opening.headline: Learn how abuse monitoring retention and model availability intersect in services that require fixed processing regions.
body: Let's assume we've built a service that must process data only within a specific region. It might seem sufficient to simply fix the processing region, but in reality, three elements move together: the location where inference is executed differs from where data is stored, prompts may be retained for a certain period to support misuse monitoring, and the number of models available within a fixed region may decrease.

In this class, we examine the regional options provided by Claude and Google, the conditions for abuse monitoring retention, and the constraints on model selection that arise when fixing a region. Finally, we follow the process by which customer support cases determine priority when regional settings conflict with performance.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: This can explain the relationship between regional processing and misuse monitoring.
The conflict between regional requirements and model availability can be distinguished.

screens.title: The region must be fixed, but data can be retained.
screens.lead: When you select three elements, scenarios where each element collides with another are presented. Open them one by one to check where the collisions occur.

visual.alt: A Venn diagram showing the overlap and conflict among three elements: regional requirements, monitoring retention, and model availability.

items.title: Regional requirement: Processing must occur only within a specific region.
items.body: There are cases where the processing region is determined by regulations, contracts, or customer requests. However, the interpretation of such requirements depends on whether they refer to the storage location or the location where inference is executed. Claude documents distinguish between inference region and storage region as two independent settings. First, it is necessary to determine whether the requirement refers to one or the other.

items.title: Misuse Monitoring: Even if a region is fixed, the prompt may remain for a certain period.
items.body: The provider may retain prompts indicating suspicious activities for a certain period in order to detect policy violations. The fact that a region is fixed does not mean such logs are deleted. Therefore, it must be separately verified where the logs are stored, how long they are retained, and who has access to them.

items.title: Model Availability: The desired model may not be available in the desired region.
items.body: Once a region is fixed, only the models available in that region can be used. If the highest-performing model is not available in the region, one must compromise either on requirements or on performance. This conflict becomes apparent only after significant development has already taken place if it is not identified during the initial design phase.

screens.outro: Let us first recall how these three elements manifest in my service.

screens.title: Consider the requirements for data processing regions
screens.lead: First, think through the question on your own and then choose an option. No input or submission is required; instead, the instructor's thoughts are organized and presented.

items.prompt: Are you referring to the storage location, or the location where inference is executed?
items.answer: They are under different control domains. The storage location is where data resides at rest, and the inference location is where the model performs computations. If the requirements document is unclear about which one is intended, it is advisable to first inquire and confirm.

items.prompt: What is the basis for this requirement—regulations, contracts, or customer requirements?
items.answer: Depending on the basis, the strictness of requirements and their possibility of exception vary. Requirements based on regulations are difficult to exempt, while customer preferences allow for negotiation. This serves as a criterion for determining which requirement takes priority when conflicts arise.

items.prompt: Is there a model that must be used?
items.answer: If a specific model is predetermined, it may directly conflict with regional requirements. Conversely, if there are multiple alternative models available, regional models can be chosen from among them, reducing potential conflicts.

screens.outro: Now I'll compare how different providers differ in their region selection options.

screens.title: Region selection option: Reasoning region and storage region
screens.lead: Select each tab to review the provider-specific regional settings and applicable scopes. Pay attention to how inference regions and storage regions are distinguished.

tabs.label: Claude: Reasoning Region
tabs.body:
`inference_geo` is a parameter that specifies the region where inference will be executed for each request. The default value is `global`, allowing execution anywhere for performance and availability reasons. If set to `us`, inference will run only on U.S. infrastructure.

The response's `usage` field also contains a `inference_geo` value, allowing you to verify exactly where the inference was executed. Within a workspace, you can restrict allowed regions using `allowed_inference_geos` and set a default value when a value is omitted from the request using `default_inference_geo`.

This parameter is supported starting with Claude 4.6 models. Specifying it with earlier models results in a 400 error. Inference dedicated to the U.S. is charged at 1.1 times the standard rate for models released after 4.6.

tabs.label: Claude: Storage region
tabs.body:
A workspace region specifies the location where data is stored and where endpoint processing such as image transformation and code execution takes place. This is set when creating a workspace and cannot be changed afterward. The currently selected option described in the document is `us`.

Inference region and storage region are two independent settings. Therefore, when asked about data residency requirements, you must separately verify whether inference processing and data storage are governed by each respective setting.

Enterprise organizations may have an inference setting that applies across the entire organization and is dedicated to the United States. This setting only governs inference processing and does not alter the location of data storage or the processing location of external services such as connectors.

tabs.label: Google Agent Platform
tabs.body:
The Google Agent Platform location documentation states that, except for data labeling tasks and experimental or preview features, all functionalities store and process data only within the region specified by the user. Regions are designated by region-specific endpoints. For example, data requested for the `europe-west4` region is sent to `https://europe-west4-aiplatform.googleapis.com`.

The Agent Platform does not support the `global` location. Furthermore, not all features are available in all regions, so it is necessary to verify that the desired feature is supported in the selected region.

screens.outro: Having verified the regional settings, I'll now examine how abuse monitoring retention policies interact with model availability.

screens.title: Misuse monitoring retention and model availability reading
screens.lead: The following is a summary comparison note based on the provider's documentation. When a highlighted section is selected, an explanation appears describing its meaning in the required design.

data.text: Gemini API states that it uses automatic detection and manual review, and reports Store the prompt, context information, and output for 55 days. Google Cloud Agent Platform can prompt Up to 90 days of retention when its classifier detects suspicious activity, and this log is recorded as Stored in the region selected by the customer, but not encrypted with the customer-managed encryption key.. OpenAI logs abuse monitoring activity as Basic retention for 30 days; approved customers may choose Modified Abuse Monitoring or no retention.. Claude's inference_geo is recorded as Supported only on models after 4.6; using it on earlier models results in a 400 error..

marks.span: Store the prompt, context information, and output for 55 days
marks.note: The Gemini API's retention policy specifies what data is retained and for how long. This includes not only the prompt but also the context provided and the model's output. You should compare these retention conditions with the retention requirements specified in the request documentation.
The Google Cloud Agent Platform logs prompts when a classifier detects suspicious activity requiring further investigation. This means data may be retained even if the region is fixed.

marks.span: Stored in the region selected by the customer, but not encrypted with the customer-managed encryption key.
marks.note: Logs remain within the selected region, satisfying regional requirements, but if there is a requirement to directly control encryption keys, then this log becomes an exception to that requirement.

marks.span: Basic retention for 30 days; approved customers may choose Modified Abuse Monitoring or no retention.
marks.note: OpenAI offers an option to exclude customer content from abuse monitoring logs upon approval. Since approval procedures are required, this should be reflected in the schedule.

marks.span: Supported only on models after 4.6; using it on earlier models results in a 400 error.
marks.note: Regional locking leads to constraints in model selection. To use US-only inference, you can only choose models within the supported model generations.

screens.outro: Now let's follow an example where the number of candidate models decreases when a region is fixed.

screens.title: Case Explanation: Conflict when a region is fixed, resulting in a reduced number of available models
screens.lead: The instructor breaks down the process of assessing conflicts in customer support service cases step by step. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step. The number of candidate models is a value assumed for illustrative purposes.

steps.title: See case
steps.body: There are customer support services that must be handled within a single region. The development team wants to use the currently most performant model. However, there may be a conflict between regional requirements and performance requirements within the same service.

steps.title: Step 1: Break down the requirements
steps.body: First, determine whether to fix the storage region and the inference region separately. The basis for this service is the customer contract, and the contract requires that processing occur within that region. Therefore, it is concluded that both storage and inference regions must be fixed.

steps.title: Step 2: Create Candidate Model List
steps.body: We begin with five candidate models, for illustrative purposes. In practice, the list is filled in based on the provider's documentation. The objective of this stage is to record the scope of selection before any region is applied.

steps.title: Step 3: Apply to Region
steps.body: Models not available in the region are removed from the candidate list, reducing the pool. For Claude, whether `inference_geo` is supported becomes the determining factor, while for Google Agent Platform, whether the feature is supported in the selected region becomes the determining factor. It's possible that the most performant model has been excluded.

steps.title: Step 4: Monitor, Store, and Verify
steps.body: Verify in documentation the retention period and storage location by provider for remaining candidates' misuse monitoring. Google Cloud retains data for up to 90 days in a selected region, Gemini API for 55 days, and OpenAI for a default of 30 days. While the regions are safeguarded, the requirement documents contrast with the fact that data within these retention periods remains stored.

steps.title: Step 5: Determine Conflict
steps.body: Whether performance or location takes priority is determined by the requirements' priority. In this case, since the contract is the basis, location takes priority. Among the remaining candidates, the most suitable model is selected through evaluation, and the rationale for the selection is documented.

steps.title: Specify the sixth-stage fee
steps.body: Instead of protecting a region, the requirements document clearly state the trade-off of reduced model selection options. It also explicitly notes the cost impact—U.S.-only inference may increase to 1.1 times the standard rate. By documenting this, we can later determine what to reevaluate when a better model becomes available. Ultimately, the decision in this case was to protect the region while choosing the best possible option available, and the key point is that we transparently recorded its limitations. This record serves as evidence when explaining to customers and as documentation during audits or reviews. Also, include in the record the alternative models that were considered and the reasons they were excluded.

screens.outro: I will conclude by summarizing the benchmarks obtained from the case study.

screens.title: Regional requirements limit model selection.
screens.lead: Summarize the core of the lesson. Recall the initial question—how local requirements, monitoring and data retention, and model availability intersect—and read through it.

paragraphs: Regional requirements do not end with a single setting. Since the location where inference is executed and the location where data is stored are controlled by separate configurations, it must first be determined which side the requirement refers to.

Even if a region is fixed, prompts may remain for a certain period due to misuse monitoring. The retention period, storage location, and encryption method should be verified separately from the provider's documentation. Even if the region is maintained, the remaining data may conflict with other requirements. For example, if data retention is also required, simply setting the region is insufficient, and the retention options must be checked separately.

When a region is fixed, only models available in that region can be used, reducing the selection options. The priority—whether performance or region—should be determined based on requirements, and this decision along with its trade-offs should be documented. Don't forget to include cost considerations. For instance, the documentation explicitly states that U.S.-only inference is charged at 1.1 times the standard rate for Claude models starting from version 4.6. Therefore, fixing a region affects not only model selection but also cost. By presenting these three impacts side by side in a single table, decision-making becomes easier. The table only needs three columns: requirement, impact, and response method.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: When regional requirements are received, verify the following three points in sequence: whether it is storage or inference, whether it is monitoring retention, and whether there is a sufficient model available for use in that region.

glossary.def: This setting performs inference or storage only within the specified region.
This is the concept of controlling the geographic location where data is stored and processed. Storage and processing must each be verified.
This involves storing prompts and outputs for a certain period to detect Oryong. Even if a region is fixed, there may still be remaining instances.
Whether the model can be used in a specific region or platform.
This is a parameter used in the Claude API to specify the region where inference will be executed per request.

misconceptions.myth: Once a region is fixed, no data remains.
misconceptions.fact: Misuse monitoring logs can be retained for a specified period within the designated region. Regional retention and no-retention are different requirements.

misconceptions.myth: All models can be used across all regions.
misconceptions.fact: The models and features available vary by region. Before selecting a model, it is necessary to verify that the model is supported in the target region.

misconceptions.myth: The inference region and storage region are the same setting.
misconceptions.fact: The Claude document describes request-specific inference regions and workspace storage regions as separate, independent settings.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: Inference region and storage region are controlled by different configurations.
Misuse monitoring retention should be individually verified even if the region is fixed.
Conflict is determined in priority based on the basis of the requirement, and the compensation is documented in the document.
closing.reflectionLead: This question is intended to encourage you to think through it on your own. It will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: What does my region's requirement refer to—storage or inference—and is there a sufficient model available within that region?
